modern: Those who fear God don’t need to fear going without. Through all these long years the Lord has always found food for his own children, whether they’ve been in the wilderness, or by the brook Cherith, or in captivity, or in the middle of famine. Up to now the Lord has given us our daily bread day by day, and we don’t doubt that he’ll keep feeding us until we need nothing more.

As for the higher and greater blessings of the covenant of grace, he will never stop supplying them as our situation requires. He remembers that he made the covenant, and never acts as if he regretted it. He remembers it when we provoke him to destroy us. He remembers to love us, keep us and comfort us, just as he promised to. He remembers every last detail of his promises, never letting one of his words fall to the ground.

We are sadly forgetful of our God, but he graciously remembers us. He can’t forget his Son, who is the Surety of the covenant, nor his Holy Spirit, who actively carries out the covenant, nor his own honor, which is bound up with the covenant. So the foundation of God stands sure, and no believer will lose his inheritance from God, which is his by a covenant of salt.

notes.term: He hath given meat unto them that fear him
notes.note: [[Ps.111.5|Psalm 111:5]]. “Meat” in the King James Bible means food of any kind.
Need, going without.
Where ravens fed Elijah during the drought ([[1Kgs.17.3-1Kgs.17.6|1 Kings 17:3–6]]).
Up to now.
God’s binding promise to save his people through Christ, freely, as a gift and not a reward.
Promised, bound himself.
Every smallest letter and mark ([[Matt.5.18|Matthew 5:18]]).

notes.term: Suffering one of His words to fall to the ground
notes.note: Letting one of his words go unfulfilled. Samuel grew, “and the LORD was with him, and did let none of his words fall to the ground” ([[1Sam.3.19|1 Samuel 3:19]]).
A guarantor: someone who promises to pay another’s debt. “Jesus was made a surety of a better testament” ([[Heb.7.22|Hebrews 7:22]]).

notes.term: The foundation of God standeth sure

notes.note: A lasting covenant that can’t be broken; salt preserves, and it was shared at covenant meals ([[Num.18.19|Numbers 18:19]]; [[2Chr.13.5|2 Chronicles 13:5]]).

modern: Joseph had been God’s providing care in human form for his brothers. All our Josephs die, and a thousand comforts die with them. Egypt was never the same to Israel after Joseph died, and the world can never again be to some of us what it was when our loved ones were alive.

But see how the pain of that sad death was eased! They had a promise that the living God would visit them. A visit from Jehovah! What a favor! What a comfort! What a heaven below! Lord, visit us today, though we are truly not worthy that you should come under our roof.

But more was promised: the Lord would bring them out. They would find a cold welcome in Egypt once Joseph was dead; in fact, it would become a house of slavery for them. But it wasn’t to be that way forever; they would come out of it by God’s rescue and march to the land of promise. We won’t weep here forever. We’ll be called home to the glory-land to join our dear ones. So “comfort one another with these words.”

notes.note: Joseph’s dying words to his brothers ([[Gen.50.24|Genesis 50:24]]).
Brothers.
God’s providing care in human form. Joseph was the means by which God kept his family alive through the famine ([[Gen.45.7|Genesis 45:7]]).
Eased, lightened.
The personal name of God in the Old Testament, printed “the LORD” in most English Bibles.

notes.term: Not worthy that thou shouldest come under our roof
notes.note: The centurion’s words to Jesus ([[Matt.8.8|Matthew 8:8]]).
No; in fact.
A place of slavery. God calls Egypt “the house of bondage” in [[Exod.20.2|Exodus 20:2]].
So, therefore.
Paul, on believers who have died and the Lord’s return ([[1Thess.4.18|1 Thessalonians 4:18]]).

modern: Other people’s portion fills their bodies and makes their children rich, but the believer’s portion is of another kind. People of this world have their treasure in this world, but people of the world to come look higher and further.

What we possess is twofold. We have God’s presence here and his likeness hereafter. Here we see the face of the Lord in righteousness, for we are justified in Christ Jesus. Oh, the joy of seeing the face of a God who is at peace with us! The glory of God in the face of Jesus Christ gives us heaven below, and it will be for us the heaven of heaven above.

But seeing doesn’t end it: we are to be changed into what we gaze on. We’ll sleep a while and then wake up to find ourselves like mirrors that reflect the beauty of our Lord. Faith looks at God with a look that transforms. The heart takes the image of Jesus into its own depths, until the character of Jesus is stamped on the soul. This is satisfaction. To see God and to be like him: what more can I want? Here David’s confident assurance is made, by the Holy Spirit, into the Lord’s promise. I believe it. I expect it. Lord, grant it. Amen.

notes.term: I shall be satisfied, when I awake, with thy likeness

notes.note: David has just described “men of the world, which have their portion in this life,” whose bellies God fills and who leave their wealth to their children ([[Ps.17.14|Psalm 17:14]]).
In the life to come.
Declared righteous by God, on the ground of what Christ has done.
A God brought back into friendship with us, at peace with us through Christ ([[2Cor.5.18|2 Corinthians 5:18]]).

notes.term: The glory of God in the face of Jesus Christ
notes.note: [[2Cor.4.6|2 Corinthians 4:6]].
The highest heaven ([[1Kgs.8.27|1 Kings 8:27]]).

notes.term: Changed into that which we gaze upon
notes.note: “We all, with open face beholding as in a glass the glory of the Lord, are changed into the same image” ([[2Cor.3.18|2 Corinthians 3:18]]).
Graciously give or grant.

modern: Come, you workers, take heart. You’re afraid you can’t draw a congregation. Try preaching a crucified, risen and ascended Savior, for this is the greatest “draw” that has ever been seen among people. What drew you to Christ but Christ? What draws you to him now but his own blessed self? If you were drawn to religion by anything else, you’ll soon be drawn away from it; but Jesus has held you, and will hold you right to the end. Why, then, doubt his power to draw others? Go with the name of Jesus to those who have been stubborn until now, and see if it doesn’t draw them.

No kind of person is beyond this drawing power. Old and young, rich and poor, uneducated and learned, depraved or kindly: all will feel its pull. Jesus is the one magnet. Let’s not think of any other. Music won’t draw people to Jesus, and neither will eloquence, logic, ceremony or noise. Jesus himself must draw people to himself, and Jesus is quite equal to the job in every case. Don’t be tempted by the gimmicks of the day; but as workers for the Lord, work in his own way, and draw with the Lord’s own cords. Draw to Christ, and draw by Christ, for then Christ will draw by you.

notes.term: I, if I be lifted up from the earth
notes.note: Jesus, speaking of the death he would die ([[John.12.32-John.12.33|John 12:32–33]]).
Something that pulls in a crowd.
Up to now.
Kindly, pleasant.
Ceremony, ritual.
Quack remedies; showy tricks that promise much and do nothing.
“I drew them with cords of a man, with bands of love” ([[Hos.11.4|Hosea 11:4]]).

modern: If this is true of literal Israel, it is much more true of spiritual Israel, God’s believing people. When saints are what they should be, they are a blessing beyond counting to the people they are scattered among.

They are like the dew, for in a quiet, unassuming way they refresh those around them. Silently but effectively, they serve the life, growth and joy of those who live with them. Coming fresh from heaven, glistening like diamonds in the sun, gracious men and women care for the weak and the overlooked, until each blade of grass has its own drop of dew. Small as individuals, together they are all that’s needed for the purposes of love the Lord carries out through them. Dewdrops refresh broad acres. Lord, make us like the dew!

Godly people are like showers that come at God’s command without asking anyone’s leave or license. They work for God whether people want it or not; they no more ask human permission than the rain does. Lord, make us just as boldly prompt and free in your service, wherever our lot is cast.

notes.term: As a dew from the Lord
notes.note: “…as the showers upon the grass, that tarrieth not for man, nor waiteth for the sons of men”: rain that comes without waiting on anyone ([[Mic.5.7|Micah 5:7]]).
The faithful few of Israel left after judgment.

notes.term: The literal Israel… the spiritual Israel
notes.note: The nation descended from Jacob, and the church: all who share Abraham’s faith ([[Gal.3.7|Galatians 3:7]]).
Too great to count.
Quiet, not drawing attention.
Effectively; actually doing the work.
Permission.
Place in life, as if given out by lot.

modern: Truth is like a huge cave we want to enter, but we can’t explore it alone. At the entrance it’s clear and bright; but if we want to go further and explore its deepest recesses, we must have a guide, or we’ll get lost. The Holy Spirit, who knows all truth perfectly, is the appointed guide of all true believers. He leads them, as they are able to bear it, from one inner chamber to another, so that they see the deep things of God, and his secret is made plain to them.

What a promise this is for a humbly inquiring mind! We want to know the truth and to enter into it. We know how prone we are to go wrong, and we feel the urgent need of a guide. We rejoice that the Holy Spirit has come and stays among us. He graciously stoops to guide us, and we gladly accept his leadership. We want to learn “all truth,” so that we won’t be one-sided and out of balance. We wouldn’t willingly be ignorant of any part of what God has revealed, in case we miss a blessing or fall into sin by it. The Spirit of God has come to guide us into all truth: let’s listen to his words with obedient hearts and follow his lead.

notes.term: He will guide you into all truth
notes.note: Jesus’ promise of the Spirit ([[John.16.13|John 16:13]]).
Travel through.

notes.term: As they are able to bear it
notes.note: “I have yet many things to say unto you, but ye cannot bear them now” ([[John.16.12|John 16:12]]).
“The Spirit searcheth all things, yea, the deep things of God” ([[1Cor.2.10|1 Corinthians 2:10]]).
“The secret of the LORD is with them that fear him” ([[Ps.25.14|Psalm 25:14]]).
Tendency to go wrong.
Graciously stoops down, in the good sense, without today’s sense of looking down on someone.
What God has made known, in Scripture.
Bring on ourselves.
Listen.

modern: Where he arranged to meet his disciples, there he would be in due time. Jesus keeps his appointments. If he promises to meet us at the mercy-seat, or in public worship, or in the ordinances, we can depend on it that he’ll be there. We may wickedly stay away from the meeting place, but he never does. He says, “Where two or three are met together in my name, there am I”; he doesn’t say “There will I be,” but “I am there already.”
Jesus is always first in fellowship: “He goeth before you.” His heart is with his people; his delight is in them; he is never slow to meet them. In all fellowship he goes ahead of us.

But he shows himself to those who come after him: “There shall ye see him.” What a joyful sight! We don’t care to see the greatest of mere men, but to see *him* is to be filled with joy and peace. And we will see him, for he promises to come to those who believe in him and to show himself to them. Rest assured that it will be so, for he does everything according to his word of promise: “As he said unto you.” Hold on to those last words, and be sure that to the end he will do for you “as he said unto you.”

notes.term: He goeth before you into Galilee
notes.note: The angel’s message to the women at the empty tomb ([[Mark.16.7|Mark 16:7]]).
An appointment to meet, especially a lovers’ meeting.
The gold lid of the ark of the covenant, where God met with his people; a picture of coming to God in prayer.
The practices Christ gave the church, chiefly baptism and the Lord’s Supper.

notes.term: “Where two or three are met together…”
notes.note: “Where two or three are gathered together in my name, there am I in the midst of them” ([[Matt.18.20|Matthew 18:20]]). Spurgeon quotes from memory.
Show himself. “I will love him, and will manifest myself to him” ([[John.14.21|John 14:21]]).
Grab hold of.

modern: “Forsaken” is a dreary word. It sounds like a funeral bell. It is the record of the sharpest sorrows and the prophecy of the worst troubles. A pit of misery gapes in that word “Forsaken.” Forsaken by one who pledged his honor! Forsaken by a friend tried and trusted for so long! Forsaken by a dear relative! Forsaken by father and mother! Forsaken by everyone! This is misery indeed, and yet it can be borne patiently if the Lord will take us up.

But what must it be like to feel forsaken by God? Think of that bitterest of cries, “My God, my God, why hast thou forsaken me?” Have we ever, to any degree, tasted the wormwood and gall of “Forsaken” in that sense? If so, let’s beg our Lord to save us from ever going through such an unspeakable sorrow again. Oh, may that darkness never return! People in their malice said of a saint, “God hath forsaken him; persecute and take him.” But it was always false. The Lord’s loving favor will make our cruel enemies eat their own words, or at least hold their tongues.

The opposite of all this is that wonderful word Hephzibah: “the Lord delighteth in thee.” This turns weeping into dancing. Let those who dreamed they were forsaken hear the Lord say, “I will never leave thee nor forsake thee.”

notes.term: Thou shalt no more be termed Forsaken
notes.note: “Thou shalt no more be termed Forsaken; neither shall thy land any more be termed Desolate: but thou shalt be called Hephzibah… for the LORD delighteth in thee” ([[Isa.62.4|Isaiah 62:4]]).
The slow ringing of a bell for a death or a funeral.
Misery, deep sorrow.
“When my father and my mother forsake me, then the LORD will take me up” ([[Ps.27.10|Psalm 27:10]]).

notes.term: “My God, my God, why hast thou forsaken me?”
notes.note: Christ’s cry from the cross ([[Matt.27.46|Matthew 27:46]]), taken from [[Ps.22.1|Psalm 22:1]].
Two bitter plants; a picture of bitter suffering ([[Lam.3.19|Lamentations 3:19]]).
Beg, plead with.

notes.term: “God hath forsaken him; persecute and take him”
notes.note: What David’s enemies said of him ([[Ps.71.11|Psalm 71:11]]).
Of the very highest degree.
Hebrew for “my delight is in her”.
“Thou hast turned for me my mourning into dancing” ([[Ps.30.11|Psalm 30:11]]).

notes.term: “I will never leave thee nor forsake thee”
notes.note: [[Heb.13.5|Hebrews 13:5]].

modern: The altar of incense is the place where saints present their prayers and praises, and it’s delightful to think of it as sprinkled with the blood of the great sacrifice. This is what makes all our worship acceptable to Jehovah: he sees the blood of his own Son, and so accepts our worship.

It’s good for us to fix our eyes on the blood of the one offering for sin. Sin mixes in even with our holy things, and our best repentance, faith, prayer and thanksgiving couldn’t be received by God if it weren’t for the merit of the atoning sacrifice. Many sneer at “the blood,” but to us it is the foundation of comfort and hope. What is on the horns of the altar is meant to be right in front of our eyes when we come near to God. The blood gives strength to prayer, and that’s why it’s on the altar’s horns. It is “before the Lord,” and so it ought to be before us. It is on the altar before we bring the incense; it is there to make our offerings and gifts holy.
Come, let’s pray with confidence, since the Victim has been offered, the merit has been pleaded, the blood is inside the veil, and the prayers of believers must be sweet to the Lord.

notes.term: The horns of the altar of sweet incense
notes.note: The four corner points of the gold altar that stood before the veil in the tabernacle. When a priest sinned, some of the sin offering’s blood was put on them ([[Lev.4.7|Leviticus 4:7]]).
The personal name of God in the Old Testament, printed “the LORD” in most English Bibles.
Worship; the honor paid to a king.
Mixes.
The sacrifice that makes peace between God and sinners by paying for sin.
Make holy; set apart for God.
The one sacrificed; here, Christ.
Inside the curtain of the Most Holy Place, where the high priest carried the blood once a year. Christ has entered heaven itself with his own blood ([[Heb.9.12|Hebrews 9:12]]).
“Let my prayer be set forth before thee as incense” ([[Ps.141.2|Psalm 141:2]]).

modern: Saints who stay faithful to God’s truth have an open door in front of them. My soul, you have decided to live and die by what the Lord has revealed in his Word, and so this open door stands in front of you.
I will go in through the open door of fellowship with God. Who will tell me no? Jesus has taken away my sin and given me his righteousness, so I may go in freely. Lord, I do, by your grace.

I also have an open door in front of me into the mysteries of the Word. I may enter into the deep things of God. Election, union with Christ, the Second Coming: all these are open to me, and I may enjoy them. No promise and no doctrine is locked away from me now.

An open door of access to God is in front of me in private, and an open door of usefulness in public. God will hear me; God will use me. A door is open for my onward march to the church above, and for my daily fellowship with saints below. Some may try to shut me in or shut me out, but it’s all in vain.
Soon I’ll see an open door into heaven: the pearl gate will be my way in, and then I’ll go in to my Lord and King and be shut in with God forever.

notes.term: I have set before thee an open door
notes.note: Christ’s words to the faithful church at Philadelphia: “I have set before thee an open door, and no man can shut it: for thou hast a little strength, and hast kept my word” ([[Rev.3.8|Revelation 3:8]]).
Close fellowship and sharing, with God or with each other. (Also the Lord’s Supper.)
Who will refuse me?
God’s choice of his people for salvation.
Being joined to Christ by faith, so that what is his becomes ours.
Christ’s return. Advent means a coming or arrival.
The right to come near. “Through him we both have access by one Spirit unto the Father” ([[Eph.2.18|Ephesians 2:18]]).
“The twelve gates were twelve pearls” ([[Rev.21.21|Revelation 21:21]]).

modern: A comfort for sick saints. They have grown faint, and they’re afraid they’ll never get up from the bed of doubt and fear; but the great Physician can both remove the disease and take away the weakness it has left behind. He will strengthen the feeble. He’ll do it in the best possible way, for it will be “in Jehovah.” Our strength is far better in God than in ourselves. In the Lord it leads to fellowship; in ourselves it would breed pride. In ourselves it would be sadly limited, but in God it knows no limit.

When strength is given, the believer uses it. He walks up and down in the name of the Lord. What a joy it is to get out and walk after an illness, and what a delight to be strong in the Lord after a time of being laid low! The Lord gives his people freedom to walk up and down, and an inner leisure to enjoy that freedom. He makes gentlemen of us: we aren’t slaves who know no rest and see no sights, but are free to travel at our ease all through Immanuel’s land.
Come, my heart, don’t be sick and sorry any longer. Jesus tells you to be strong and to walk with God in holy contemplation. Obey his word of love.

notes.term: They shall walk up and down in his name
notes.note: [[Zech.10.12|Zechariah 10:12]].
Comfort.
Christ. “They that be whole need not a physician, but they that are sick” ([[Matt.9.12|Matthew 9:12]]).
The personal name of God in the Old Testament, printed “the LORD” in most English Bibles. Spurgeon gives the verse’s “in the LORD” its full sense.
Outdoors, out and about.
Being laid low, completely worn out.
Christ’s own country. Immanuel, “God with us,” is a name of Christ ([[Matt.1.23|Matthew 1:23]]); “thy land, O Immanuel” ([[Isa.8.8|Isaiah 8:8]]).
Quiet, thoughtful attention to God.

modern: Here we read of the true circumcision.

Notice its author: “The Lord thy God.” He alone can deal effectively with our heart and take away its worldliness and filth. Making us love God with all our heart and soul is a miracle of grace that only the Holy Spirit can work. We must look to the Lord alone for this and never be satisfied with anything less.

Notice where this circumcision is done. It isn’t in the flesh but in the spirit. It is the essential mark of the covenant of grace. Love for God is the indelible sign of the chosen people; by this secret seal, the believer is assured that he is one of those chosen by grace. We must make sure we trust in no outward ritual, but are sealed in heart by the work of the Holy Spirit.

Notice what the result is: “that thou mayest live.” To be carnally minded is death. In overcoming the flesh we find life and peace. If we set our minds on the things of the Spirit, we’ll live. Oh, that Jehovah our God would complete his gracious work on our inner nature, so that in the fullest and highest sense we may live to the Lord.

notes.term: The Lord thy God will circumcise thine heart
notes.note: [[Deut.30.6|Deuteronomy 30:6]].
Circumcision was the outward sign of God’s covenant with Abraham. The Bible speaks of a circumcision of the heart, the inner change it pointed to ([[Rom.2.28-Rom.2.29|Romans 2:28–29]]).
Effectively; actually doing the work.
Worldliness; the desires of our fallen human nature.
Worked.
God’s binding promise to save his people through Christ, freely, as a gift and not a reward.
A mark that can’t be rubbed out.
God’s chosen people, Abraham’s true children by faith.
Those God has chosen freely: “There is a remnant according to the election of grace” ([[Rom.11.5|Romans 11:5]]).

notes.term: To be carnally minded is death
notes.note: “To be carnally minded is death; but to be spiritually minded is life and peace” ([[Rom.8.6|Romans 8:6]]).

notes.term: Mind the things of the Spirit
notes.note: Set our minds on them ([[Rom.8.5|Romans 8:5]]).
The personal name of God in the Old Testament, printed “the LORD” in most English Bibles.

modern: Though we are called by the Lord’s name, we are still men and women who go wrong. What a mercy it is that our God is ready to forgive! Whenever we sin, let’s hurry to our God’s mercy-seat to ask for pardon.

We are to humble ourselves. Shouldn’t we be humbled by the fact that after receiving so much love, we still sin? Lord, we bow before you in the dust and confess our terrible ingratitude. Oh, the shame of sin! Oh, the sevenfold shame of it in people as favored as we have been!
Next, we are to pray for mercy, for cleansing, for rescue from the power of sin. Lord, hear us right now, and don’t shut out our cry.
In this prayer we are to seek the Lord’s face. He has withdrawn from us because of our faults, and we must beg him to come back. Lord, look on us in your Son Jesus, and smile on your servants.
Along with this must go our own turning from evil. God can’t turn to us unless we turn from sin.
Then comes the triple promise of hearing, pardon and healing. Our Father, grant us these at once, for our Lord Jesus Christ’s sake.

notes.term: If my people, which are called by my name
notes.note: God’s answer to Solomon’s prayer at the dedication of the temple ([[2Chr.7.14|2 Chronicles 7:14]]).
Going wrong, sinning.
The gold lid of the ark of the covenant, where God met with his people; a picture of coming to God in prayer.
Sin; break God’s law.
Admit, confess.
Disgrace, shame.
Seven times over; complete.
Jeremiah’s complaint: “When I cry and shout, he shutteth out my prayer” ([[Lam.3.8|Lamentations 3:8]]).
Beg, plead with.

modern: A gracious promise! It’s a great joy to me to confess my Lord. Whatever my faults may be, I’m not ashamed of Jesus, and I’m not afraid to declare the teachings of his cross. Lord, I have not hidden your righteousness in my heart.

What a sweet prospect this verse sets before me! Friends forsake me and enemies gloat, but the Lord doesn’t disown his servant. No doubt my Lord will acknowledge me even here, and give me new signs of his favor. But a day is coming when I must stand before the great Father. What bliss to think that Jesus will confess me then! He will say, “This man truly trusted me and was willing to be insulted for my name’s sake, and so I acknowledge him as mine.” The other day a great man was made a knight, and the Queen gave him a jeweled garter; but what of that? It will be an honor beyond all honors for the Lord Jesus to confess us in the presence of the divine Majesty in heaven. Never let me be ashamed to own my Lord. Never let me give in to a cowardly silence or allow a fainthearted compromise. Shall I blush to own him who promises to own me?

notes.term: Whosoever therefore shall confess me before men
I have not hid thy righteousness within my heart

notes.note: Gloat, rejoice in triumph.
Acknowledge as his.
Signs, proofs.
Insulted, put to shame.
The badge of the Order of the Garter, England’s highest order of knighthood. The Queen was Victoria.

modern: We live because we are united with the Son of God. As the God-man Mediator, the Lord Jesus lives by the self-existent Father who sent him, and in the same way we live by the Savior who has made us alive. He who is the source of our life is also what keeps it going. Life is kept going by feeding. We must sustain the spiritual life with spiritual food, and that spiritual food is the Lord Jesus. Not his life, or death, or offices, or work, or word alone, but himself, including all these. We feed on Jesus himself.

This is pictured for us in the Lord’s Supper, but we actually enjoy it when we meditate on our Lord, believe in him with a faith that makes him our own, take him into ourselves by love, and absorb him by the power of the inner life. We know what it is to feed on Jesus, but we can’t say it or write it. Our wisest course is to practice it, more and more. We are urged to eat abundantly, and it will do us endless good to do so when Jesus is our food and drink.
Lord, I thank you that what my new life can’t do without is also its greatest delight. So right now, I feed on you.

notes.term: He that eateth me, even he shall live by me

notes.note: Because of, by the power of.
Christ, fully God and fully man, who stands between God and us to bring us together ([[1Tim.2.5|1 Timothy 2:5]]).
Depending on nothing outside himself for his being.
Made alive.
Food; what keeps life going.
His roles, chiefly prophet, priest and king.
Faith that takes Christ as its own.
Take in and make part of ourselves.
Urged, begged.
Food. “My flesh is meat indeed, and my blood is drink indeed” ([[John.6.55|John 6:55]]).

modern: Jesus has made the life of those who believe in him as certain as his own. As surely as the Head lives, the members live too. If Jesus hasn’t risen from the dead, then we are dead in our sins; but since he has risen, all believers are risen in him. His death has put away our sins and loosed the chains that held us under the death sentence. His resurrection proves our justification: we are acquitted, and mercy says, “The Lord hath put away thy sin, thou shalt not die.”

Jesus has made the life of his people as eternal as his own. How can they die as long as he lives, since they are one with him? Because he dies no more, and death has no more power over him, they won’t go back to the graves of their old sins, but will live to the Lord in newness of life. Believer, when you are under great temptation and afraid you’ll fall one day by the hand of the enemy, let this reassure you. You will never lose your spiritual life, for it is hidden with Christ in God. You don’t doubt your Lord’s immortality; so don’t think he’ll let you die, since you are one with him. The argument for your life is his life, and you can have no fear about that; so rest in your living Lord.

notes.term: Because I live, ye shall live also
If Jesus has not risen from the dead
notes.note: “If Christ be not raised, your faith is vain; ye are yet in your sins” ([[1Cor.15.17|1 Corinthians 15:17]]).
He “was raised again for our justification” ([[Rom.4.25|Romans 4:25]]).
Pardoned, declared free of guilt.

notes.term: “The Lord hath put away thy sin, thou shalt not die”
notes.note: Nathan to David ([[2Sam.12.13|2 Samuel 12:13]]).

notes.term: Death hath no more dominion over him
notes.note: [[Rom.6.9|Romans 6:9]].
[[Rom.6.4|Romans 6:4]].
[[Col.3.3|Colossians 3:3]].
So, therefore.

modern: Holy awe of God’s Word is out of fashion. People think they are wiser than the Word of the Lord, and sit in judgment on it. “So did not I, because of the fear of God.” We accept the inspired Book as infallible, and prove our respect for it by our obedience. We aren’t terrified of the Word, but we have a child’s awe of it. We don’t fear its penalties, because we fear its commands.

This holy fear of the commandment produces the restfulness of humility, which is far sweeter than the recklessness of pride. It becomes a guide in our movements: a brake when we are going downhill and a spur when we are climbing. Kept from evil and led into righteousness by our reverence for the command, we gain a quiet conscience, which is a well of wine; a sense of being free from responsibility, which is like life from the dead; and a confidence that we are pleasing God, which is heaven below. The ungodly may ridicule our deep reverence for the Word of the Lord, but what of it? The prize of our high calling is comfort enough for us. The rewards of obedience make us scorn the scoffer’s scorn.

notes.term: He that feareth the commandment shall be rewarded
notes.note: “Whoso despiseth the word shall be destroyed: but he that feareth the commandment shall be rewarded” ([[Prov.13.13|Proverbs 13:13]]).
Little valued, out of fashion.

notes.term: “So did not I, because of the fear of God”
notes.note: Nehemiah, refusing to burden the people as earlier governors had ([[Neh.5.15|Nehemiah 5:15]]).
Incapable of error.
Like a son or daughter toward a parent.
A brake: a shoe or chain put on a cart wheel to slow it going downhill.

notes.term: The prize of our high calling
notes.note: “I press toward the mark for the prize of the high calling of God in Christ Jesus” ([[Phil.3.14|Philippians 3:14]]).
“How long… will the scorners delight in their scorning?” ([[Prov.1.22|Proverbs 1:22]]).

modern: Times of weeping are good for sowing: we don’t want the ground too dry. Seed soaked in the tears of earnest concern will come up all the sooner. The salt of prayerful tears will give the good seed a flavor that keeps the worm away: truth spoken with awe-filled earnestness has a double life in it. Instead of stopping our sowing because of our weeping, let’s double our efforts, because the season is so favorable.

Our heavenly seed couldn’t rightly be sown with laughter. Deep sorrow and concern for other people’s souls go far better with godly teaching than anything like flippancy. We have heard of men who went to war light-heartedly, but they were beaten; and it’s mostly the same with those who sow in that style.

Come, then, my heart, keep sowing in your weeping, for you have the promise of a joyful harvest. You will reap. You yourself will see some result of your work. It will come to you in so large a measure that it will give you joy, which a poor, withered, scanty harvest wouldn’t do. When your eyes are dim with silver tears, think of the golden grain. Bear the present toil and disappointment cheerfully, for harvest day will repay you in full.

notes.term: They that sow in tears shall reap in joy

notes.note: Full of awe, solemn (not “terrible”).
Favorable.
Rightly, suitably.
Lightness; flippancy where seriousness is called for.

notes.term: Went to war with a light heart
notes.note: A phrase made famous by the French prime minister Émile Ollivier, who said in 1870 that he accepted war with Prussia “with a light heart.” France was quickly beaten.
Grain of any kind, such as wheat or barley.
Repay, reward.

modern: To be left uncorrected would be a deadly sign: it would prove that the Lord had said, “He is given unto idols, let him alone.” God grant that such may never be our lot! Unbroken prosperity is something to make us fear and tremble. All those God tenderly loves, he rebukes and disciplines; those he has no regard for, he lets fatten themselves without fear, like bullocks for the slaughter. It is in love that our heavenly Father uses the rod on his children.

Yet notice, the correction is “in measure.” He gives us love without measure, but discipline “in measure.” Under the old law no Israelite could be given more than “forty stripes save one,” which ensured careful counting and limited suffering; and it’s the same with each afflicted member of the household of faith: every stroke is counted. It is the measure of wisdom, the measure of sympathy, the measure of love, that regulates our discipline. Far be it from us to rebel against arrangements so divine. Lord, if you stand by to measure the bitter drops into my cup, it’s for me to take that cup cheerfully from your hand and drink as you direct, saying, “Thy will be done.”

notes.term: I will correct thee in measure
notes.note: “Though I make a full end of all nations whither I have scattered thee, yet will I not make a full end of thee: but I will correct thee in measure” ([[Jer.30.11|Jeremiah 30:11]]).

notes.term: “He is given unto idols, let him alone”
notes.note: God’s verdict on Ephraim: “Ephraim is joined to idols: let him alone” ([[Hos.4.17|Hosea 4:17]]). Spurgeon quotes from memory.

notes.term: Such may never be our portion
notes.note: That may never be our lot, what falls to us.

notes.term: As many as God tenderly loves He rebukes and chastens
notes.note: “As many as I love, I rebuke and chasten” ([[Rev.3.19|Revelation 3:19]]).
Young bulls fattened to be killed. “Ye have nourished your hearts, as in a day of slaughter” ([[Jas.5.5|James 5:5]]).
God’s discipline, the way a father corrects a child.
Thirty-nine lashes. The law allowed no more than forty ([[Deut.25.3|Deuteronomy 25:3]]), so the count stopped one short to be safe. Paul received it five times ([[2Cor.11.24|2 Corinthians 11:24]]).
Discipline, correction.
Arrangements; what God has appointed.

modern: Lord, save me from my sins. Your name, Jesus, encourages me to pray like this. Save me from my past sins, so that their habit doesn’t hold me captive. Save me from the sins of my temperament, so that I’m not the slave of my own weaknesses. Save me from the sins that are always in front of my eyes, so that I don’t lose my horror of them. Save me from secret sins, sins I don’t notice because I lack light. Save me from sudden and surprising sins: don’t let me be swept off my feet by a rush of temptation. Save me, Lord, from every sin. Don’t let any wrongdoing rule over me.

You alone can do this. I can’t snap my own chains or kill my own enemies. You know temptation, for you were tempted. You know sin, for you carried its weight. You know how to help me in my hour of conflict; you can save me from sinning, and save me when I have sinned. Your very name promises that you will do this, and I pray, let me prove the prophecy true today. Don’t let me give way to temper, or pride, or despondency, or any form of evil; but save me into holiness of life, so that your name, Jesus, may be glorified in me abundantly.

notes.term: He shall save his people from their sins
notes.note: The angel to Joseph: “thou shalt call his name JESUS: for he shall save his people from their sins” ([[Matt.1.21|Matthew 1:21]]). The name means “the LORD saves.”
Sins that come from our own temperament and make-up.
“Cleanse thou me from secret faults” ([[Ps.19.12|Psalm 19:12]]).
Lack.

notes.term: Let not any iniquity have dominion over me

notes.note: “In all points tempted like as we are, yet without sin” ([[Heb.4.15|Hebrews 4:15]]).
Help, come to the aid of.
Prove true.
Feeling low and discouraged.

modern: Work for the Lord often begins on a small scale, and it’s none the worse for that. Weakness trains faith, brings God near and wins glory for his name. Treasure the promises of increase! The mustard seed is the smallest of seeds, and yet it becomes a treelike plant, with branches where the birds of heaven nest. We may begin with one, and that “a little one,” and yet it will “become a thousand.” The Lord is great at the multiplication table. How often he said to his lone servant, “I will multiply thee!” Trust in the Lord, you ones and twos, for he will be among you if you are gathered in his name.

“A small one.” What could be more contemptible in the eyes of those who count heads and weigh forces? Yet this is the seed of a great nation. Only one star shines out at first in the evening, but soon the sky is crowded with countless lights.

And we don’t need to think the prospect of increase is far off, for the promise is, “I Jehovah will hasten it in his time.” There will be no premature rush, like what we see at overexcited meetings; it will all be in due time, and yet there will be no delay. When the Lord hurries, his speed is glorious.

notes.term: A little one shall become a thousand

notes.note: “The least of all seeds: but when it is grown, it is the greatest among herbs, and becometh a tree, so that the birds of the air come and lodge in the branches thereof” ([[Matt.13.31-Matt.13.32|Matthew 13:31–32]]).
Nest, shelter.
God’s promise to Abraham ([[Gen.17.2|Genesis 17:2]]; [[Gen.22.17|22:17]]).

notes.term: In the midst of you if you are gathered in His name

notes.note: Contemptible, not worth noticing.
The core something grows from.
The personal name of God in the Old Testament, printed “the LORD” in most English Bibles. Spurgeon gives the verse’s “I the LORD” as “I Jehovah.”
Too early.

modern: This is a promise being pleaded, and so it teaches us twice over. Anything the Lord God has spoken we should receive as certainly true, and then plead it at the throne.
Oh, how sweet to quote what our own God has spoken! How precious to use a “therefore” that the promise suggests, as David does in this verse!

We don’t pray because we doubt, but because we believe. To pray in unbelief doesn’t suit the Lord’s children. No, Lord, we can’t doubt you: we are persuaded that every word of yours is a sure foundation for the boldest hope. We come to you and say, “Do as thou hast said.” Bless your servant’s house. Heal our sick; save our wavering ones; bring back those who wander; strengthen those who live in your fear. Lord, give us food and clothing according to your word. Make our undertakings succeed, and especially bless our efforts to make your gospel known in our neighborhood. Make our servants your servants, and our children your children. Let the blessing flow on to future generations, and as long as any of our family remains on earth, may they stay true to you. O Lord God, “let the house of thy servant be blessed.”

notes.term: Thou, O Lord God, hast spoken it
notes.note: The end of David’s prayer after God promised him a lasting house ([[2Sam.7.29|2 Samuel 7:29]]).
“Therefore now let it please thee to bless the house of thy servant” ([[2Sam.7.29|2 Samuel 7:29]]).
Not fitting, out of character.
From the same prayer of David ([[2Sam.7.25|2 Samuel 7:25]]).
Clothing.
Make our efforts succeed.
Household servants, whom many homes had in Spurgeon’s day.

modern: Righteousness is often costly to the person who sticks to it at any risk, but in the end it will pay its own expenses and bring in an infinite profit. A holy life is like sowing seed: much goes out, and it seems to be buried in the soil, never to be gathered up again. We are mistaken when we look for an immediate harvest; but the mistake is very natural, for it seems impossible to bury light. Yet light is “sown,” says the text. It lies hidden: no one can see it; it is sown. We are quite sure that one day it must show itself.

We are fully sure that the Lord has set a harvest for those who sow light, and they’ll reap it, each one for himself. Then their gladness will come: sheaves of joy for seeds of light. Their heart was upright before the Lord, though people gave them no credit for it, and even criticized them; they were righteous, though those around them condemned them as fault-finding. They had to wait, as farmers wait for the precious fruit of the earth; but the light was sown for them, and gladness was being prepared for them by the Lord of the harvest.
Courage, brothers! We don’t need to be in a hurry. Let’s keep possession of our souls with patience, for soon our souls will possess light and gladness.

notes.term: Light is sown for the righteous

notes.note: At any risk.
Hidden, present but not yet seen.
Show itself.
Criticized, blamed.
Fault-finding, quick to judge.
Farmers. “The husbandman waiteth for the precious fruit of the earth, and hath long patience for it” ([[Jas.5.7|James 5:7]]).
“In your patience possess ye your souls” ([[Luke.21.19|Luke 21:19]]).

modern: Steadiness in the fear and faith of God will make a person like a wall of bronze that no one can batter down or break. Only the Lord can make such people; but we need them in the church and in the world, and especially in the pulpit.

This age of shams will fight tooth and nail against uncompromising people of truth. Nothing seems to offend Satan and his offspring like decisiveness. They attack holy firmness the way the Assyrians besieged fortified cities. The joy is that they can’t prevail against those God has made strong in his strength. Others, carried about by every wind of doctrine, only need to be blown on, and away they go; but those who love the doctrines of grace, because they have the grace of the doctrines, stand like rocks in the middle of raging seas.

Where does this steadiness come from? “I am with thee, saith the Lord”: that is the true answer. Jehovah will save and rescue faithful souls from all the enemy’s attacks. Hosts are against us, but the Lord of hosts is with us. We don’t dare budge an inch, for the Lord himself holds us in our place, and there we will stay forever.

notes.note: A fortified wall of bronze; God’s promise to Jeremiah ([[Jer.15.20|Jeremiah 15:20]]).
Fakes, pretenses.
His offspring, his followers ([[Gen.3.15|Genesis 3:15]]).
“Sennacherib king of Assyria came up against all the fenced cities of Judah” ([[2Kgs.18.13|2 Kings 18:13]]).

notes.term: Carried about with every wind of doctrine
notes.note: [[Eph.4.14|Ephesians 4:14]].
The teaching that salvation is God’s free gift from start to finish: his choosing, Christ’s dying, the Spirit’s calling and keeping.
From where.
The personal name of God in the Old Testament, printed “the LORD” in most English Bibles.
Armies, and God as the commander of heaven’s armies. “The LORD of hosts is with us” ([[Ps.46.7|Psalm 46:7]]).
Remain, stay.

modern: See how the Bible opens: “In the beginning God.” Let your life open the same way. Seek with your whole soul, first and foremost, the kingdom of God as the place of your citizenship, and his righteousness as the character of your life. As for the rest, it will come from the Lord himself without your worrying about it. Everything needed for this life and for godliness “shall be added unto you.”

What a promise this is! Food, clothing, home and so on: God takes it on himself to add them to you while you seek him. You mind his business, and he will mind yours. When you buy more important goods, you get the paper and string thrown in; and in just the same way, all the earthly things we need we’ll have thrown in with the kingdom. Whoever is an heir of salvation won’t die of starvation; and whoever clothes his soul with the righteousness of God can’t be left by the Lord with a naked body. Away with gnawing worry! Set your whole mind on seeking the Lord. Greed is poverty and anxiety is misery; trust in God is an estate, and likeness to God is a heavenly inheritance. Lord, I seek you; let me find you.

notes.term: Seek ye first the kingdom of God
notes.note: [[Matt.6.33|Matthew 6:33]]. “All these things” are the food, drink and clothing of the verses before.
[[Gen.1.1|Genesis 1:1]].
“His divine power hath given unto us all things that pertain unto life and godliness” ([[2Pet.1.3|2 Peter 1:3]]).
Clothing.
Shops wrapped what you bought in paper tied with string, at no extra charge.
Gnawing, burdensome worry.
Greed; wanting what isn’t yours.
Property, a fortune.
“Ye shall seek me, and find me, when ye shall search for me with all your heart” ([[Jer.29.13|Jeremiah 29:13]]).

modern: For the sake of his chosen ones, the Lord holds back many judgments and shortens others. In great times of trouble the fire would devour everything, if the Lord didn’t damp down the flame out of regard for his elect. So while he saves his elect for Jesus’ sake, he also preserves the human race for the sake of his chosen.

What an honor this puts on the saints! How diligently they ought to use their influence with their Lord! He will hear their prayers for sinners and bless their efforts for their salvation. He blesses believers so that they may be a blessing to those who don’t believe. Many a sinner is alive because of the prayers of a mother or wife or daughter whom the Lord regards.

Have we used rightly the remarkable power the Lord entrusts to us? Do we pray for our country, for other lands and for our age? In times of war, famine and plague, do we stand out as intercessors, pleading that the days may be shortened? Do we mourn before God over the outbursts of unbelief, error and immorality? Do we beg our Lord Jesus to shorten the reign of sin by hurrying his own glorious appearing? Let’s get on our knees, and never rest until Christ appears.

notes.term: For the elect’s sake those days be shortened
notes.note: Jesus, speaking of a coming time of great tribulation ([[Matt.24.21-Matt.24.22|Matthew 24:21–22]]).
God’s chosen people.
Troubles, sufferings.

notes.term: To whom the Lord has respect
notes.note: Whom the Lord regards with favor.
Remarkable, unusual.
Plague, deadly disease.
People who pray for others.
Unbelief; rejecting Christianity.
Immorality; throwing off moral restraint.
Beg, plead with.
“Looking for that blessed hope, and the glorious appearing of the great God and our Saviour Jesus Christ” ([[Titus.2.13|Titus 2:13]]).

modern: Three choice blessings will be ours in the land of glory.

“His servants shall serve him.” No other lords will oppress us; no other service will distress us. We will serve Jesus always, perfectly, without weariness and without error. This is heaven to a saint: to serve the Lord Christ in everything. To be acknowledged by him as his servant is our soul’s high ambition for eternity.

“And they shall see his face.” This makes the service delightful; in fact, it is service’s present reward. We will know our Lord, for we will see him as he is. To see the face of Jesus is the greatest favor the most faithful servant of the Lord can ask. What more could Moses ask than “Let me see thy face”?

“And his name shall be in their foreheads.” They gaze on their Lord until his name is photographed on their brows. They are acknowledged by him, and they acknowledge him. The secret mark of inner grace develops into the public signature of a confessed relationship.
Lord, give us these three things in their beginnings here, so that we may have them in all their fullness in your own home of bliss!

notes.note: [[Rev.22.3-Rev.22.4|Revelation 22:3–4]].
Acknowledged, claimed as his own.

notes.term: We shall see Him as He is
notes.note: “We shall be like him; for we shall see him as he is” ([[1John.3.2|1 John 3:2]]).
Moses asked, “I beseech thee, shew me thy glory” ([[Exod.33.18|Exodus 33:18]]), and God answered, “Thou canst not see my face” ([[Exod.33.20|33:20]]). Spurgeon gives the sense of the request.
Still a new wonder in Spurgeon’s day: an image fixed by light.
A signature written in someone’s own hand, especially a king’s.
Home, dwelling.

modern: Because of our ignorance, we aren’t fully aware of our sins of ignorance. Yet we can be sure they are many, both things we have done and things we have left undone. We may be doing in all sincerity, as a service to God, something he never commanded and can never accept.

The Lord knows every one of these sins of ignorance. This may well alarm us, since in justice he will hold us to account for these wrongs; but on the other hand, faith spots comfort in this fact, for the Lord will make sure that stains we don’t see will still be washed away. He sees the sin so that he may stop seeing it, by throwing it behind his back.

Our great comfort is that Jesus, the true Priest, has made atonement for the whole congregation of the children of Israel. That atonement guarantees the pardon of unknown sins. His precious blood cleanses us from all sin. Whether our eyes have seen it and wept over it or not, God has seen it, Christ has atoned for it, and the Spirit bears witness to its pardon; and so we have a threefold peace.
My Father, I praise your divine knowledge, which not only sees my sins but provides an atonement that frees me from their guilt, even before I know I am guilty.

notes.term: It shall be forgiven them; for it is ignorance
notes.note: The law’s provision for sins the people committed without knowing ([[Num.15.24-Num.15.25|Numbers 15:24–25]]).
Sins of doing what we shouldn’t, and of not doing what we should.

notes.term: Require these trespasses at our hand
notes.note: Hold us to account for these wrongs.
“Thou hast cast all my sins behind thy back” ([[Isa.38.17|Isaiah 38:17]]).
Making peace between God and sinners by paying for sin.

notes.term: All the congregation of the children of Israel
His precious blood cleanses us from all sin
notes.note: “The blood of Jesus Christ his Son cleanseth us from all sin” ([[1John.1.7|1 John 1:7]]).
Sins, wickedness.

modern: Pharaoh has a people, and the Lord has a people. They may live side by side and seem to fare alike, but there is a dividing line between them, and the Lord will make it plain. The same thing won’t happen to everyone forever; there will be a great difference between the people of the world and the people Jehovah has chosen.

This may happen in times of judgment, when the Lord becomes the sanctuary of his saints. It is very plain to see in the conversion of believers, when their sin is put away while unbelievers remain under condemnation. From that moment they become a distinct race, come under a new discipline and enjoy new blessings. From then on, their homes are free from the terrible swarms of evils that defile and torment the Egyptians. They are kept from the pollution of lust, the bite of worry, the corruption of lies and the cruel torment of hatred, which devour many families.

Rest assured, tested believer, that though you have your troubles, you are saved from swarms of worse ones that infest the homes and hearts of those who serve the Prince of this world. The Lord has put a division; make sure you keep up the division in spirit, aim, character and company.

notes.term: I will put a division between my people and thy people
notes.note: God’s word to Pharaoh before the plague of flies, which would not touch the land of Goshen where Israel lived ([[Exod.8.22-Exod.8.23|Exodus 8:22–23]]).

notes.term: One event happen alike to all
notes.note: “All things come alike to all: there is one event to the righteous, and to the wicked” ([[Eccl.9.2|Ecclesiastes 9:2]]).
The personal name of God in the Old Testament, printed “the LORD” in most English Bibles.
A place of safety. “He shall be for a sanctuary” ([[Isa.8.14|Isaiah 8:14]]).
Easy to see.
“There came a grievous swarm of flies into the house of Pharaoh” ([[Exod.8.24|Exodus 8:24]]).
Any strong desire, especially a sinful one, not only sexual desire.
Satan, “the prince of this world” ([[John.12.31|John 12:31]]).

modern: What a great joy this is! He who has purified us with the blood of Jesus will also cleanse us with the water of the Holy Spirit. God has said it, and so it must be: “Ye shall be clean.” Lord, we feel our uncleanness and mourn over it, and it’s cheering to be assured from your own mouth that we will be clean. Oh, that you would make quick work of it!

He will rescue us from our worst sins. The risings of unbelief, the deceitful desires that wage war against the soul, the vile thoughts of pride, and Satan’s suggestions to blaspheme the sacred name: all these will be so cleansed away that they never return.

He will also cleanse us from all our idols, whether of gold or of clay: our impure loves, and our excessive love for what is pure in itself. What we have made an idol of will either be broken away from us, or we will be broken away from it.

It is God who speaks of what he himself will do. So this word is established and sure, and we may boldly look for what it guarantees us. Cleansing is a covenant blessing, and the covenant is ordered in all things and sure.

notes.term: Then will I sprinkle clean water upon you
notes.note: God’s promise to Israel in exile ([[Ezek.36.25|Ezekiel 36:25]]), followed by the promise of a new heart ([[Ezek.36.26|36:26]]).
Quick.

notes.term: The deceitful lusts which war against the soul
notes.note: “Fleshly lusts, which war against the soul” ([[1Pet.2.11|1 Peter 2:11]]); “deceitful lusts” ([[Eph.4.22|Ephesians 4:22]]).
Speak with contempt of God.
Cleansed, cleared out.
Made an idol of.

notes.term: Ordered in all things and sure
notes.note: David’s last words: “an everlasting covenant, ordered in all things, and sure” ([[2Sam.23.5|2 Samuel 23:5]]).

modern: A good assurance, this! No doubt it was based on a promise, whispered inwardly in the psalmist’s heart, which he grabbed hold of and enjoyed. Is my case like David’s? Am I depressed because the enemy insults me? Are there crowds against me and few on my side? Does unbelief tell me to lie down and die in despair, a defeated, disgraced man? Are my enemies beginning to dig my grave?

What then? Shall I give in to the whisper of fear and give up the fight, and all hope with it? Far from it. There is life in me yet: “I shall not die.” Strength will come back and remove my weakness: “I shall live.” The Lord lives, and I will live too. My mouth will be opened again: “I shall declare the works of Jehovah.” Yes, and I’ll speak of this present trouble as another example of the wonder-working faithfulness and love of the Lord my God. Those who would happily measure me for my coffin had better wait a bit, for “the Lord hath chastened me sore, but he hath not given me over unto death.” Glory to his name forever! I am immortal until my work is done. Until the Lord wills it, no tomb can close on me.

notes.term: I shall not die, but live

notes.note: Insults.
The personal name of God in the Old Testament, printed “the LORD” in most English Bibles. Spurgeon gives the verse’s “the LORD” as “Jehovah.”

notes.term: The Lord lives, and I shall live also
notes.note: “Because I live, ye shall live also” ([[John.14.19|John 14:19]]).
